findings.reason: as written the implementer builds the wait to read `section_readiness` and `section_gate_blockers` only, so the fully-gated branch silently reads unheld and the queue launches work the roadmap holds.
findings.text: the paragraph states "A section held by its own plan's unpassed gate is reported separately, in the roadmap's `section_gate_blockers`, and a wait reads both", but `split_unpassed_gates` (`reckon/roadmap.py:887-901`) returns the section-scoped list only while some implementable section is left unnamed by an open gate (`if declared - named: ... return plan_holding, naming`); when every implementable section is gate-named it returns `plan_holding, []`, so the gate lands in the plan-level `gate_blockers` and `section_gate_blockers` is empty — and because gates are not in the `section_readiness` guard at `reckon/roadmap.py:3578`, such a plan also carries no `section_readiness`. A wait derivation reading only the two structures the sentence names therefore sees no hold at all on a plan the roadmap reports as `blocked` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3451-3480`), and can launch a request on a section held behind an unpassed gate — the plan's instruction "answered per section, never from the plan-level summary" would exclude the very field that carries this hold

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the paragraph this review was scoped to verify resolves fully: `section_gate_blockers` is attached at `reckon/roadmap.py:3525` and produced by `split_unpassed_gates` (`reckon/roadmap.py:854`), the `section_readiness` guard is exactly `if section_dependency_blockers or mapped_edges or decision_section_blockers` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3578`), `_readiness_by_slug` does keep one verdict per plan (`{slug: readiness}`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:3094-3124`), `RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES` is `("complete", "completed", "done", "landed", "promoted")` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1023`), `MANIFEST_STATUSES` excludes the other four (`reckon/crew/reports.py:127-140`), `run_ids` is public at `reckon/ledger.py:1019`, and `_promoted_run_ids` wraps it (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:550-561`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §8's done-when carries measurable arms (DAG-order launch, cycle refusal naming both refs, mixed section/`--after` cycle refusal, unknown-section refusal, blocked/failed closure moving a waiter to `blocked-upstream`, an unlanded `complete` waiter staying `awaiting-upstream`) plus a declared negative arm ("declares B's §2 done before queuing, and the request goes straight to `queued`"), and the positive arms fail on today's code.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §8 names no scratchpad or node-local path; its write paths are repository modules and a new test file, and the plan's own evidence target (`docs/evidence/archive/a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan-landed.html`, §14) is a durable path under the repository.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed text introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and its prose states mechanism rather than changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the new sentence says a section held by its plan's unpassed gate is reported in `section_gate_blockers` and that a wait reads both that and `section_readiness`, but the roadmap moves that hold to the plan-level `gate_blockers` when every implementable section is gate-named, leaving `section_gate_blockers` empty and `section_readiness` unattached.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 carries one deliverable, the cross-plan/cross-project DAG respect for the queue; the cycle check is part of that same mechanism, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §8's declared `plan-section-depends-on` edge to s2 resolves, and the section's Owners name the modules it writes (`queue_admission.py`, `dispatch_admission.py`, `crew_dispatch_commands.py`, `node.py`, `plan_review.py`) with each cited symbol present in the tree (`_readiness_rows` at `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1056`, `_readiness_by_slug` at `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:3094`, `parse_plan_ref` at `reckon/_schema.py:276`).
